brand.title: Exercise Decoder
brand.intro: Pick exercises by body part — not by confusion. Choose 1–2 movements per area, match them to your level, and let the muscle do the work. Dumbbell and bodyweight options included.

video.label: Start here
video.title: How to use the Exercise Decoder
video.caption: A quick walkthrough before you pick your exercises.

groups.name: Glutes
groups.howTo: Pick 1–2 glute exercises per workout. Build them slowly and make the glute do the work — not your low back.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Step-Up
exercises.why: Builds glutes and legs while training balance. Scale by box height, tempo, or adding a pause at the top.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.why: Single-leg glute and quad builder that needs no weights. Use a chair or bench for the rear foot.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: A hinge pattern for glutes and hamstrings using only your bodyweight. Move slow and feel the stretch.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Glute Bridge
exercises.why: A top glute activator you can do anywhere. Great for warming up or finishing a glute block with high reps.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Hip Thrust
exercises.why: The same strong glute activation pattern as weighted hip thrusts — no equipment needed. Pause at the top and drive through your heels.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.why: Based on the hip thrust family, one of the strongest glute activation patterns in the supplied EMG data.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge
exercises.why: Based on the glute bridge, a top glute activator that lets you train the glutes with very little setup.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: A high-return hinge for glutes and hamstrings. Useful when you want shape without needing machines.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.why: Excellent for glutes and legs at the same time. Great when you want curves and leg tone.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.why: A practical glute and leg builder that also trains balance and single-leg control.

groups.name: Quads
groups.tagline: For toned legs and stronger squats
groups.howTo: Choose 1 squat or single-leg pattern. You do not need every quad exercise in the same workout.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Step-Up
exercises.why: Quad-focused when you take a longer step and drive through the front heel.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
exercises.why: A knee-friendly single-leg quad builder that also trains glutes and balance.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.why: The foundation quad builder. Keep heels down, ribs stacked, and sit between your hips.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.why: Based on squat variations that ranked highest for quad activation. Simple, coachable, and dumbbell friendly.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Squat
exercises.why: A strong quad-focused squat option when you have two dumbbells and want more load than a goblet squat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.why: A high-return quad and glute exercise that makes lighter dumbbells feel challenging.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.why: A strong leg-toning option that is easy to scale by changing box height, load, or tempo.

groups.name: Hamstrings
groups.tagline: For the back of the legs and glute tie-in
groups.howTo: Pick one hinge. Move slow. Feel the stretch. Keep the spine quiet and the hips doing the work.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Glute Bridge
exercises.why: Also trains hamstrings when you push through heels and keep tension on the way down.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bodyweight RDL
exercises.why: Challenges hamstrings, glutes, and balance in one move. Use a wall or chair for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: The best no-equipment hinge for hamstrings and glutes. Keep a soft knee and long spine.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: One of the best dumbbell choices for hamstrings, glutes, and posterior-chain shape.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.why: Based on the deadlift, which ranked at the top for average hamstring activation in the supplied testing.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell RDL
exercises.why: A strong hamstring and glute movement with extra balance and hip-control demand.

groups.name: Calves
groups.howTo: Calves usually respond best to controlled reps, a full stretch, and progressive loading.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bodyweight Calf Raise
exercises.why: Doubles the load per leg without needing weights. Great on a step for extra range.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
exercises.why: Full-range calf work with no equipment. Pause at the top and control the stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise
exercises.why: Based on heavy calf raise data. Use a full range of motion and pause at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.why: Great when dumbbells are limited because one leg makes the load feel heavier.

groups.name: Chest
groups.howTo: Presses build strength. Fly variations help you feel the chest. Keep shoulders down and ribs controlled.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Floor Fly
exercises.why: An isolation-style chest squeeze using only your arms on the floor. Best done slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.why: Upper-chest friendly and easier to control. Use a bench, counter, or wall to scale difficulty.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Press
exercises.why: Based on the dumbbell incline press, a top upper-chest activator in the supplied chest data.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.why: Based on the dumbbell bench press, one of the strongest mid-chest activation exercises tested.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.why: A strong isolation choice from the chest data. Best done light, controlled, and pain-free.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.why: A no-equipment chest builder that scales well for busy nurses training at home.

groups.name: Back
groups.tagline: For posture, width, and a smaller-looking waist
groups.howTo: Back training is huge for nurses: charting, patient care, fatigue, and rounded posture make this area matter.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Bodyweight Row
exercises.why: Single-arm row using a door anchor, table, or suspension trainer. Great for lat focus.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Superman Row
exercises.why: Prone pulling pattern for upper back and posture — no equipment beyond the floor.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.why: A bodyweight row using a sturdy table, bar, or TRX. Builds lats and mid-back for posture.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.why: A practical dumbbell lat builder based on the top pull-up and chin-up patterns from the back data.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.why: One of the strongest dumbbell choices for mid-back and lower-trap activation.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.why: A great upper-back option when you want support for the low back while still training the posture muscles.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: Based on the rack pull, one of the highest overall back activators tested. This is the dumbbell-first version.

groups.name: Shoulders
groups.tagline: For upper-body shape and waist contrast
groups.howTo: These are coach additions for physique balance. They help create shape around the waist, hips, and upper body.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Lateral Raise
exercises.why: Side delt shape work using arm abduction against gravity. Strict form beats heavy load here.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Rear Delt Fly
exercises.why: Rear shoulder and posture work using only arm rotation. Great after long shifts.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Y Raise
exercises.why: Builds traps and rear shoulders lying face-down. No weights — squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.why: A bodyweight overhead press pattern for shoulders. Hips high, head between hands, control the descent.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.why: Builds side-shoulder shape, which helps create a stronger shoulder-to-waist contrast.

levels.A: Leaning or Slow Tempo Lateral Raise

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
exercises.why: Builds the rear shoulder and supports better posture after long shifts and charting.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Trap Raise
exercises.why: Based on the prone trap raise, which performed extremely well for mid and lower traps.

groups.name: Triceps
groups.howTo: The triceps create most of the shape in the upper arm. Pick one direct triceps exercise when arms are a focus.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
exercises.why: Overhead triceps extension lying on the floor. Targets the long head with no equipment.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.why: Hands close together to emphasize triceps. Scale with incline or knee variations.

exercises.name: Bench Dip
exercises.why: Direct triceps work using a bench or chair. Keep shoulders down and elbows tracking back.

exercises.name: Overhead Dumbbell Extension
exercises.why: Based on overhead triceps extension patterns that target the long head of the triceps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
exercises.why: Based on the skull crusher, a strong direct triceps movement from the supplied data.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.why: A dumbbell alternative based on rope and cable extension patterns. Best with strict form and a squeeze.

groups.name: Biceps
groups.howTo: Pulling movements already train biceps. Add curls when you want direct arm work.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Concentration Curl
exercises.why: Leg-resisted curl using your own body as resistance. Squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: Doorway Towel Curl
exercises.why: Anchor a towel in a door for resistance curls. A practical home biceps option.

exercises.name: Underhand Inverted Row
exercises.why: Chin-up grip on a bodyweight row builds biceps along with back. Use a table or bar.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl
exercises.why: Based on barbell curl data and translated into the dumbbell version most nurses can use anywhere.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.why: A strong arm exercise because it challenges the biceps in a stretched position.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.why: Builds arm thickness and forearm shape while staying joint-friendly for many lifters.
